text: On the IPO question: you cannot apply for an Indian IPO with $10 — the minimum application size is usually Rs 15,000 and you need an Indian demat account, PAN and a UPI mandate. text: To answer your IPO question: with $10, you can apply for an IPO, but if allotted, you must have the full cash ready to cover the purchase price; if you don't have enough, the application is rejected. speaker: Kimi K3
text: NVDA's 14% drop today on 2.2x volume with RSI at 15 is the most oversold this name has been since 2022, yet the fundamentals haven't cracked — Q3 operating margins actually expanded to 66.2% on 96% revenue growth, and the last three quarters all beat EPS by 5-8%. The street's price targets still cluster $180-280, implying 43-123% upside from $125, but eight firms just downgraded to Hold/Neutral post-earnings, so the near-term catalyst path is murky. For your $100 fractional position, zero commission means you can average down cleanly, but the 20% short-term capital gains tax on any profit under a year cuts the net; at a 30% marginal rate you'd keep 70 cents of every dollar gained. I'd treat this as a multi-year compounder, not a 10x-in-months lottery ticket — the 10-year CAGR of 49% says patience gets paid, but the -89% max drawdown says you need stomach for it.
